includeTranscriptSegments.description: ⏱️ Include timestamped segments — Return the transcript as timestamped segments in addition to the plain text. Turn off for a flatter table.

name: meta-ad-library-scraper
description: Meta Ad Library Scraper. Scrape Facebook and Instagram ads from Meta's Ad Library by keyword or advertiser page: ad text, headline, call to action, link, image and video URLs, format, platforms and run dates. One flat row per ad, with a hard cap. Export data, run via API, schedule runs.

queries.description: 🔍 Search keywords — Words or brand names to search the Ad Library for, one per line. Every ad whose text, advertiser or link matches is returned.

pageIds.description: 📄 Facebook page IDs — Numeric page IDs to pull every ad of one advertiser, instead of searching by keyword. The ID is the number in an ad's Ad Library link, and it is also returned as pageId on every row.

country.description: 🌍 Country — Two-letter country code of the audience the ads were shown to, for example US, GB, DE. Meta indexes ads per country, so this changes which ads exist, not just how they are filtered.

activeStatus.description: 🟢 Ad status — Whether to return ads that are still running, ads that have stopped, or both.

adType.description: 🗳️ Ad type — All ads, or only the political and social-issue shelf. Meta publishes spend, impressions and reach for that shelf and for nothing else, so the spend, impressionsText and reachEstimate columns only carry numbers here.

mediaType.description: 🖼️ Media type — Keep only ads of one format. Meta applies this itself, so it changes which ads are fetched and therefore what you pay for.

platforms.description: 📱 Platforms — Limit to ads shown on particular Meta surfaces. Leave empty for all of them.

startDate.description: 📅 Ads started after — Only ads that began running on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

endDate.description: 📅 Ads started before — Only ads that began running on or before this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

maxAds.description: 💯 Maximum ads — Hard cap for the whole run. It is checked before every request, so the run stops at this number and never bills you past it.

maxAdsPerQuery.description: Maximum ads per keyword or page — Optional per-target cap, so one broad keyword cannot eat the whole run.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy — Meta serves the Ad Library to residential addresses only; from a datacentre address it answers with an empty response. Leave this on the default unless you know why you are changing it.

name: au-grocery-scraper
description: Coles, Woolworths & ALDI Scraper. Scrape Australian grocery prices from Coles, Woolworths and ALDI in one run: price, was-price, discount, unit price, stock, category, ingredients and nutrition. Compare the three chains on one row, watch price changes, or list stores near a postcode.

keywords.description: 🔎 What to look up — Products to look up in every selected chain — milk, nappies, tim tam, olive oil. Each keyword is searched in Coles, Woolworths and ALDI and comes back in one table.

categories.description: 📂 Category pages — Whole aisles instead of a keyword. Paste a Coles category link such as https://www.coles.com.au/browse/dairy-eggs-fridge/milk, or an ALDI category key such as 970000000. Woolworths does not answer category requests from an anonymous visitor, so use keywords for it.

chains.description: 🏪 Chains — Which supermarkets to read. Leave all three on to compare them.

output.description: 📤 What a row should be — One product per row gives every product of every chain separately. One comparison per row puts the same product from the different chains on one row with the Coles, Woolworths and ALDI price next to each other and names the cheapest. One store per row lists the Coles, Woolw

maxProductsPerKeyword.description: 💯 Products per keyword, per chain — How deep to go in each chain for each keyword. Thirty is a fast look; raise it to sweep a whole aisle.

productUrls.description: 🔗 Product URLs — Specific products instead of, or alongside, a search. Paste Coles, Woolworths or ALDI product links — the chain is recognised from the link.

postcode.description: 📍 Postcode — An Australian postcode, used to find Coles, Woolworths and ALDI stores near it in the store mode. Coordinates can be given instead.

latitude.description: Latitude — Coordinates instead of a postcode, e.g. -33.8688. Both latitude and longitude must be given.

colesStoreId.description: 🏬 Coles store number — Set it and Coles rows come back with the aisle the product sits in and the quantity that store has on the shelf, instead of the national range. The number is in the URL of your store on the Coles site.

includeNutrition.description: 🥗 Ingredients, allergens and nutrition — Woolworths ships the label with the product and it is always included. Coles keeps it on the product page, so each Coles product needs one extra request, charged as a separate add-on. ALDI publishes no label data at all.

maxNutritionLookups.description: Maximum label lookups per run — A ceiling on the extra Coles requests, so a large sweep cannot surprise you.

watchName.description: 🔔 Watch name — deliver only what changed — Give this run a name — weekly-shop, dairy — and every later run under the same name returns only products whose price moved, that went on or off special, that came back in stock, or that are new. Leave empty to get everything found, every time.

deliverBaseline.description: 📥 Deliver everything on the first run of a watch — The first run of a new watch has nothing to compare against. Leave this on to receive the current prices as the starting point; turn it off to start silently and hear only about movements from now on.

resetWatch.description: ♻️ Forget the prices this watch remembers — Wipe this watch's memory and start a new baseline on this run.

onSpecialOnly.description: 🏷️ Only products on special — Keep only products with a was-price or a special flag.

minDiscountPercent.description: 📉 Minimum discount, % — Keep only products discounted by at least this much. Zero means no minimum.

maxPrice.description: 💲 Maximum price, AUD — Ignore anything dearer than this. Zero means no limit.

inStockOnly.description: 📦 Only what is in stock — Drop products the chain reports as unavailable.

matchMode.description: 🔗 How strictly to match products across chains — Same brand only ever compares like with like: the same brand, or the three house brands against each other (Coles, Woolworths, ALDI's Farmdale and friends). Equivalent also matches a different brand of the same size and wording — wider, and every row

maxItems.description: Maximum rows per run — A hard ceiling on what one run delivers and bills.

concurrency.description: Parallel requests — How many chain requests to run at once.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration — Apify Proxy is on by default with residential addresses, because Coles often refuses datacenter traffic (on 16 September 2026 it stopped answering the datacenter pool altogether). With this default the Actor still tries the cheaper datacenter pool first and moves a site to resi

name: sports-odds-api
description: Sports Betting Odds API — Pinnacle, DraftKings & Arbitrage. Moneyline, spread and total odds per book — Pinnacle sharp lines with the risk limit it accepts, DraftKings, Kalshi — plus arbitrage and value bets calculated across books, opening lines, props and futures. NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, college, soccer, UFC, tennis. No API key.

mode.description: 🧭 What to get — Odds — moneyline, spread and total for every game, per book, with opening lines and movement. Props — player and game props from DraftKings for every game. Futures — championship, division, award and season-win markets. Prediction markets — Kalshi game contracts with traded probabil

leagues.description: 🏆 Leagues — One or more leagues. Odds, props and Kalshi contracts are matched game by game. For a league that is not in this list, put its ESPN path (for example soccer/eng.2) in Custom leagues below.

customLeagues.description: Custom leagues (ESPN paths) — Any ESPN league path not in the list above, e.g. soccer/eng.2 (Championship), soccer/ger.2, basketball/nbl. The game list comes from ESPN; DraftKings, Pinnacle and Kalshi prices are added when they carry that league.

daysAhead.description: 📅 Days ahead — Games from today (UTC) up to this many days ahead (ignored when dates are set below). 0 = today only.

dateFrom.description: 📅 From date — YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Optional. Games are kept by their kick-off time in UTC.

dateTo.description: 📅 To date — YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Optional; at most 60 days after the start.

markets.description: 📊 Markets — Odds mode: which game lines to output. Spread is the run line in MLB and the puck line in NHL; soccer moneylines carry a draw price.

books.description: 📚 Sources — Pinnacle — the sharp reference book the rest of the market prices against, with the risk limit it will accept on each market. DraftKings — live prices straight from the sportsbook feed. ESPN — every provider ESPN carries for the game (DraftKings, Bet365 where present) with opening lines

oddsFormat.description: 🔢 Odds format — How the homePrice/awayPrice/overPrice… fields are written. Decimal odds and implied probabilities are always included as separate fields.

outputFormat.description: 🧱 Row layout — Flat — one row per game × market × book, spreadsheet-friendly. Nested — one row per game with all books inside and the best price per outcome.

includeOpeningLines.description: 📈 Opening lines and movement — Fetch the opening line and price for each game (one extra request per game) and compute how far the line and prices have moved.

includeAlternateLines.description: ➕ Alternate spreads and totals — Add DraftKings' alternate lines as extra rows (market alternate-spread / alternate-total).

includeFinished.description: 🏁 Include finished games — Odds mode: keep games that are already final (closing lines, if a source still carries them). Prediction-markets mode: keep settled contracts.

includeEdges.description: 💰 Find arbitrage and value bets — Adds edge rows on top of the prices: arbitrage — the best price on each side, taken from whichever book offers it, when together they guarantee a profit; value — a book paying more than Pinnacle’s vig-free probability says the outcome deserves. Needs at least two s

minEdgePercent.description: 📉 Smallest edge worth reporting, % — Prices move by a tick constantly, so anything under half a percent is noise a bettor would pay away in the spread. Raise it to see only the big disagreements.

eventIds.description: 🎯 Only these games — ESPN event ids (the eventId field of any row, or the number in an ESPN game URL). Leave empty for every game in the date range.

propCategories.description: 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Prop categories — Props mode: keep only categories whose name contains one of these, e.g. Passing, TD Scorers, Points, Batter. Empty = every player and game prop category (this can be thousands of rows per game).

maxPropsPerGame.description: Props per game cap — Stop after this many prop rows for one game.

futuresCategories.description: 🏆 Futures categories — Futures mode: keep only categories whose name contains one of these, e.g. Futures, Awards, Wins, Playoffs. Empty = every futures-type category.

kalshiSeries.description: 🎲 Kalshi series tickers — Prediction-markets mode: series tickers to pull directly, e.g. KXNFLGAME, KXUCLGAME, KXATPMATCH. Leagues selected above are added automatically.

maxItems.description: 💯 Maximum rows — Stop after this many rows in the run. The default of 18 keeps a first trial run at about $0.05 — raise it once you like the output.

concurrency.description: Parallel requests — How many requests run at once.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration — Not needed: every source answers Apify's own servers directly. Set only if a source starts refusing. Leave it off unless a source starts refusing you: DraftKings answers Apify's own servers but blocks datacenter proxies, so switching the proxy on can cost you its prices rather

includeRunSummary.description: 🧾 Add a free summary row at the end of the run — One extra free row with the run's totals: rows delivered, free rows, what was charged and how much in US dollars. It carries type "notice", so a filter on your data rows skips it.

name: tennis-scores-api
description: Tennis Scraper & Scores API — ATP, WTA, Live, Stats. Tennis scraper on SofaScore data: live scores, schedules, results, match statistics, point by point, betting odds, ATP and WTA rankings, player profiles and draws for ATP, WTA, Challenger, ITF and UTR. One flat row per match. Export to CSV or JSON, run via API, schedule, or call from AI agents.

mode.description: 🎾 What to get — Schedule: every match in a date window — upcoming, live and played — for the tours you pick. Live: only what is on court right now. Results: completed matches with scores and winners, newest first. Match: one named match with optional statistics, point-by-point and head-to-head. Pla

dateFrom.description: 📅 Date — Day to list matches for, YYYY-MM-DD in UTC. Leave empty for today. Only a rolling window of roughly two months around today is available from this source.

daysBack.description: ⬅️ Days back — How many days before the date to include (0–14). Use 1 in Results mode to get yesterday's finished matches as well as today's.

days.description: ➡️ Days ahead — How many days after the date to include (0 = that day only, up to 14). Use 6 for a whole tournament week.

tours.description: 🏆 Tours — Which circuits to keep. ATP and WTA are preselected because they are what most buyers want and they keep a run small; the Challenger and ITF levels add several hundred matches a day. Grand Slams appear under ATP and WTA. One request covers the whole day whatever you pick here, so narrowin

status.description: 🎯 Keep only — Filter by state. Played keeps everything that produced a result, including retirements and walkovers — the row's own status column says which it was. Not played is the opposite: cancelled, postponed, interrupted.

matchType.description: 👥 Singles or doubles — Doubles rows carry both partners in homePartners / awayPartners.

playerName.description: 🔎 Only matches of a player — Keep only matches where a player's name contains this text, e.g. Sinner. Used by schedule, live, results and player modes. A surname is enough.

matchIds.description: 🆔 Match ids or URLs (match mode) — FlashScore match ids such as pnSMQFtQ, or the match URLs they come from. Ids are in the matchId column of any schedule or results run. They can only be looked up while the match is inside the source's rolling week.

playerIds.description: 🧑 Player ids (player and WTA modes) — Player ids from the homePlayerId / awayPlayerId columns, or numeric WTA ids for the official WTA modes. Use Search mode to find them by name.

query.description: 🔍 Name to search (search mode) — Player name, e.g. Alcaraz. Returns the ids you can paste into the fields above.

rankingTour.description: 🥇 Rankings tour (rankings mode) — Which official ranking to read. Each list comes from that tour's own site, so one failing does not take the other down.

rankingDiscipline.description: 🥇 Rankings: singles or doubles — Doubles lists can share a rank between two players; such rows carry tied: true and the next rank is skipped, exactly as the tour publishes it.

rankingTop.description: 🥇 Ranking rows per tour — How many players from the top of each list. One hundred per page, so 100 is one request per tour.

includeStatistics.description: 📊 Add match statistics to every match — Aces, double faults, first and second serve, break points, winners, points and games won — for the whole match and per set, around 65 numbers. Available once a match is under way. One extra request and one extra billed row per match.

includePointByPoint.description: 🎯 Add point-by-point to every match — Every game of every set with its point sequence, who served and who won the game. For modelling and trading; leave off if you only need scores.

includeHeadToHead.description: 🤝 Add head-to-head to every match — Recent form of both players and their previous meetings, grouped by surface. This is the heaviest extra — well over a hundred kilobytes per match — so use it on a short list, not a whole day.

maxMatches.description: 💯 Maximum rows per run — Safety cap across every mode, and the main control over what a run costs. Fifty rows of ATP and WTA is a normal day.

maxMatchesPerPlayer.description: Matches per player (player and WTA modes) — How many of a player's matches to return. In player mode the search walks back day by day, so a wider Days back finds more.

concurrency.description: Parallel requests — How many requests to run at once. Three is gentle and enough for a day of matches; raise it only when the extras are on for a long list.

proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration — Off by default, on purpose. This source answers ordinary datacenter addresses, and one day of matches is well over a megabyte — pushing that through residential addresses would cost more in bandwidth than the rows themselves. If a run is ever refused, the Actor retries through

wtaDiscipline.description: 🏆 WTA ranking table — Singles or doubles list, used by the WTA official — rankings mode.

wtaYear.description: 📅 WTA season — Limit the official WTA match history to one season, e.g. 2025. Leave empty for the most recent matches.

playerNames.description: 🔍 WTA player names — Players to look up in the official WTA modes, by name, e.g. Sabalenka. Each name is resolved against the tour's own player list.

newestFirst.description: 🆕 Most recent first — In the official WTA match history, start from the latest matches instead of the start of the player's career.
